looks.name: The Classic Navy
looks.why: Dark horn buttons keep a navy suit quiet and business-like, and a navy lining keeps the inside as clean as the outside.

looks.name: The Charcoal Workhorse
looks.why: Charcoal goes with every shirt you own. Dark horn buttons and a grey lining keep it sharp with no fuss.

looks.name: The Boardroom Stripe
looks.why: A peak lapel and dark horn buttons sharpen a stripe. The lining stays quiet - the cloth does the talking.

looks.name: The Double-Breasted
looks.why: A peak lapel gives double-breasted its classic shape. Dark horn buttons keep the stronger silhouette timeless.

looks.name: The Black Tie
looks.why: Covered buttons and a shawl collar are the classic black-tie signals, and a black lining keeps it formal.

looks.name: The Navy Blazer
looks.why: Gold metal buttons are the classic blazer signal. A paisley lining adds personality only you know is there.

looks.name: The Summer Tan
looks.why: Light horn buttons and a cream lining keep a tan suit feeling light and easy.

looks.name: The Country Check
looks.why: Corozo is a natural nut button that suits earthy checks. The paisley lining picks up the brown in the cloth.

looks.name: The Light Grey Wedding
looks.why: Shell buttons and a soft pink lining give a light grey suit a gentle, dressed-up feel.

looks.name: The Burgundy Statement
looks.why: Dark horn buttons ground the strong colour, and the paisley lining carries the statement inside.

looks.name: The Green Herringbone
looks.why: Brown horn and a camel lining warm up green cloth - an easy smart-casual combination.

looks.name: The Cream Summer
looks.why: Bone buttons stay light, and a pale blue lining is a fresh surprise against cream.

tips.buttons: Metal buttons are the classic blazer choice; horn tones it down toward a suit jacket.
tips.linings: A blazer can carry a bolder lining - paisley or even a picture lining.

tips.buttons: Dark horn buttons ground a strong colour; brighter buttons would compete with the cloth.
tips.linings: A paisley that picks up the cloth colour carries the statement inside. Tone-on-tone calms it down.

tips.buttons: Light horn, corozo or bone buttons suit warm cloth; dark buttons can sit heavy on tan.
tips.linings: Cream, camel or a warm paisley lining keeps the warm feel.

tips.buttons: Bone, shell or light horn buttons keep cream light. Dark buttons give it more contrast.
tips.linings: Pale blue, sand or cream linings keep it fresh for summer.

tips.buttons: Shell or light horn buttons keep light grey soft; dark horn sharpens it.
tips.linings: A soft colour inside - pink, sky or cream - suits a wedding. Grey keeps it business.

tips.buttons: The cloth already has a pattern, so plain horn or corozo buttons usually sit best.
tips.linings: A plain lining in a colour from the pattern works well; a print would fight with the cloth.

tips.buttons: Dark horn or corozo buttons keep a dark solid suit quiet and business-like. Metal buttons push it toward a blazer look.
tips.linings: Tone-on-tone keeps it strict. A quiet paisley adds personality that only shows when the jacket comes off.

tips.buttons: Horn and corozo are the safe, classic buttons for most cloths.
tips.linings: Tone-on-tone is always safe; a print adds personality inside.
